name: The Humane League (Founders Pledge, 2019)
summary: Corporate campaigns for cage-free eggs and better broiler welfare. Founders Pledge's 2019 analysis extrapolates from case studies to all of THL's 2015–2018 campaign wins, counts the hen-years they moved out of battery cages (broilers and chicks as fixed fractions of one), credits THL only with the years it brought each policy forward, and divides by THL's whole budget for those years. It is more than ten times its peers because Founders Pledge credits THL's 2015–2018 corporate wins with about 61 hen-years (or their equivalent in broilers and chicks) moved out of battery cages per dollar of its whole budget, counting five years for each won policy, each hen-year at the shared 17.5 SADs.

rows.label: Discount rate on the years counted and the wait
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: every future benefit is discounted at "Next year's good counts less by", the wait until a policy takes effect included. Founders Pledge counts the years brought forward at face value, so the evaluator view uses 0.

rows.label: Years from winning the cage-free policies until they take effect
rows.explainer: Ours. The cage-free policies THL won in 2015–2018 set deadlines mostly in 2020–2026 (Sodexo 2020 in the US and 2025 worldwide, Chick-fil-A 2026; Chicken Watch), so the hens' lives change several years after the win. Our judgment: 6 years, 3 to 9. Founders Pledge doesn't model the wait; the evaluator view doesn't discount it.

rows.label: Years from winning the broiler policies until they take effect
rows.explainer: Ours. The broiler policies (Better Chicken Commitment) won in 2016–2018 carry a 2024 deadline. Our judgment: 6 years, 4 to 8. Founders Pledge doesn't model the wait; the evaluator view doesn't discount it.

rows.label: Years from winning the chick-culling policy until it takes effect
rows.explainer: Ours. United Egg Producers pledged in 2016 to end culling by 2020 or as soon as in-ovo sexing was commercially available, which in the US came later. Our judgment: 4 years, 2 to 10. Founders Pledge doesn't model the wait; the evaluator view doesn't discount it.

rows.label: Hen-years per dollar from the international cage-free policies
Share of the international hens that start in enriched rather than battery cages
rows.explainer: Battery cages have been banned in the EU since 2012 and in the UK, so most of the international hens move from enriched cages to aviaries, a smaller change. Some (Mexico, other non-EU countries) were still in battery cages. Range is ours.

rows.label: Broilers raised under better welfare standards per dollar
rows.explainer: The broiler part of Founders Pledge's result taken back to birds: Founders Pledge counted each broiler as a tenth of a hen-year; here each counts with the site's shared figure for a broiler raised to Better Chicken Commitment standards instead.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar: hens out of battery cages (and Founders Pledge's chick-culling equivalents)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge counts hen-years; the site counts suffering. Each hen-year moved from a battery cage to an aviary averts the shared 17.49 suffering-adjusted days (Ambitious Impact's figure as ACE used it in 2025, a 2024 SAD figure), the same figure every model uses for this change. Hens that start in enriched cages go in the next row instead.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar: broilers under better standards and hens out of enriched cages
rows.explainer: Each broiler raised to Better Chicken Commitment standards averts the shared 0.64 suffering-adjusted days, and each hen-year moved from an enriched cage to an aviary the shared 3.05 (ACE's 2025 figures, 2025 SADs). On the same 2024 basis, Founders Pledge's weight for a broiler (a tenth of a hen-year, 1.75 SADs) is about twice the shared figure (0.86), so broilers count for less here than in Founders Pledge's result.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar: hens out of battery cages
rows.explainer: The site's species step: the hen weight built into the 2024 SAD figure (46% of a person's) taken out, which leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar: broilers and hens out of enriched cages
rows.explainer: The same for the 2025 broiler figure, with the 2025 hen weight (35% of a person's) taken out. The evaluator view divides by the 2024 weight its conversion is pinned to.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar
Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Advocacy is mostly people, so staff pay is usually most of the budget. We haven't seen this charity's breakdown; the default is the same guess we use for other animal advocacy groups. Range is ours.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Campaigners, researchers and negotiators could typically earn considerably more in comparable for-profit roles. Range is ours.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Your value, shared with every model built on an organisation's past average (Your values: "How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far"): Founders Pledge divides THL's whole 2015–2018 budget by the campaign wins of those years, an average; the next dollar does less than the average dollar did, since an organisation pursues its best opportunities first. 50% by default (our judgment), from 18% to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, counted as a chicken's. With credit by share of resources on, times the share of the full cost paid in cash. The headline turns this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain. A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row above).
